title: New Captains, New Coach: Ireland and Afghanistan Set for Five-Match ODI Showdown
excerpt: Ireland ride the momentum of a historic T20I series sweep of India into their first ODIs in 15 months, while Afghanistan begin life under new skipper Rahmat Shah as both teams eye 2027 World Cup qualification.
body:
• Ireland’s first ODI series in 15 months begins August 5 under newly appointed head coach Gary Wilson, the first Irish-born coach in over 30 years.
  • Rahmat Shah takes over as Afghanistan’s ODI captain after Hashmatullah Shahidi resigned following a 3-0 series loss to India in June.
  • India T20I hero Jai Moondra earns his maiden ODI squad call-up alongside uncapped pacer Byron McDonough.
  • Both teams are positioning for 2027 ODI World Cup qualification, with Ireland currently 11th in the ICC ODI rankings.

Ireland and Afghanistan will begin a five-match ODI series at the Cricket Club Ground in Bready on August 5, with both teams entering under new leadership and carrying the weight of recent results against India into a series that could shape their 2027 World Cup qualification campaigns.

Fresh Starts on Both Sides

For Ireland, this is Gary Wilson’s first series in charge as head coach. The 40-year-old former Ireland wicketkeeper, who earned 292 caps during a 15-year international career, was appointed on June 29 — one day after Ireland completed a stunning 2-0 T20I series sweep of India at Stormont, Belfast. Wilson replaced Heinrich Malan, who stepped down despite having a contract running into early 2027, with both parties agreeing the timing was right ahead of the World Cup qualification cycle. Wilson is the first Irish-born head coach of the men’s team in over three decades.

Afghanistan, meanwhile, will be led by Rahmat Shah after Hashmatullah Shahidi resigned the captaincy following a 3-0 ODI series defeat to India in June. The 33-year-old Rahmat has served as vice-captain in Tests and ODIs since 2021 and is Afghanistan’s leading run-getter in the 50-over format, with 4,121 runs at an average of 35.22, according to Cricinfo.

Squad Shake-ups and New Faces

Ireland captain Paul Stirling returns after missing the India T20I series through injury. The squad also features several fresh faces: Jai Moondra, who became an overnight sensation during the India series by taking a wicket with his first ball in international cricket, gets his chance in the 50-over format. Byron McDonough, a 24-year-old medium-pacer who helped Leinster Lightning win the Inter-Provincial Limited Overs Cup, earns his maiden Ireland call-up. Ben Calitz, whose powerful middle-order batting impressed in the T20Is, enters the ODI squad for the first time.

Afghanistan have bolstered their fast-bowling stocks by recalling Fazalhaq Farooqi and Yamin Ahmadzai. Farooqi has been in form in the Lanka Premier League, picking up five wickets in two matches for Dambulla Sixers. Mohammad Nabi is absent, opting for the Global Super League with Guyana Amazon Warriors, while Mujeeb Ur Rahman is sidelined by injury.

“We have selected a squad that is reflective of the way in which we want to play. We want to be dynamic and look for opportunities to put pressure on the opposition.”

— Gary Wilson, Ireland Men’s Head Coach

World Cup Qualification in Focus

Both teams have their eyes on the 2027 ODI World Cup, expanded to 14 teams. Ireland sit 11th in the ICC ODI rankings, just outside the automatic qualification cut-off, and will likely need to navigate a global qualifier next year. These are their first ODIs in 15 months, making the five-match series a rare extended runway. For Afghanistan, ranked eighth, the series is an opportunity to reset under new captaincy after a difficult stretch against India. The squad retains key match-winners in Rashid Khan and Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who takes on the vice-captaincy.

Riding the India Wave

Ireland’s confidence will be sky-high after the India T20I result — their first-ever series win over India in any format, which also snapped India’s 16-series T20I winning streak. Moondra and Matt Hollard, the two debutants who each took three wickets in the second T20I, embodied the fearlessness Wilson will want to carry into ODI cricket. Harry Tector, who scored a half-century on his 100th T20I cap, provides experienced firepower alongside Stirling and Andrew Balbirnie.

Afghanistan will be looking to find form quickly. Their transition away from Shahidi’s captaincy — he led in 55 ODIs from January 2022 — adds uncertainty, though Shahidi remains in the squad as a regular player.

The first two ODIs will be played at Bready on August 5 and 7, before the series shifts to Stormont in Belfast for matches on August 10, 12, and 15. All games start at 10:45 AM local time. For diaspora cricket fans who followed India’s summer tours closely, this series offers a compelling subplot: how two teams that recently faced India, with dramatically different outcomes, redirect their energies against each other in Irish conditions.
